A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ADM/SAM flatness study. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–B support comparison; changed experimental settings are identifiable.

before.justification: V1 reports original diffusion-model experiments on CIFAR-10, LSUN Tower, and FFHQ, including generation quality, flatness, exposure bias, and quantization results.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds IP/pEMA comparisons, adversarial-attack results, and additional quantization evaluations.

M1.justification: The ADM architecture, SAM objective and updates, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Post-hoc EMA appears as an additional averaging comparator and combination, without redesigning the core ADM/SAM method.

E1.justification: The three datasets, image resolutions, and unconditional generation task remain unchanged. Section 6 adds an adversarial-input test scenario; cross-domain generation and few-shot personalization are only proposed future applications.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds IP, IP+EMA, and IP+SWA to the three-dataset FID comparison, although IP already participated in v1's flatness and exposure-bias analyses. Appendix B.3 additionally evaluates pEMA and SAM+pEMA, substantially expanding the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported FFHQ training budget from 120K to 200K steps and extends the stated SWA averaging schedule to all datasets. Added protocols include loss-maximizing adversarial perturbations, sevenfold noise amplification, and fixed-seed comparisons extending quantization to 4 bits. The PDFs do not establish which retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds adversarial robustness testing in Table 5, fixed-seed quantization sensitivity through 4-bit precision in Figure 9, and pEMA flatness/quantization analysis in Appendix B.3. The earlier exposure-bias and loss-landscape analyses, including appendix Figures 7–8, remain.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses that Figure 4 did not use a fixed random seed and reports fixed-seed sampling for Figure 9. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces FFHQ SAM FIDs of 31.89/12.43 at 20/100 steps with 11.59/5.29 and also changes its SAM+EMA and SAM+SWA results. The changed training budget prevents interpreting these as same-setting gains. V2 adds IP, pEMA, adversarial, and 4-bit results; Figure 9 reports 4-bit FIDs of 202.33 for ADM and 41.45 for SAM.

T1.justification: Corollary 2 and Appendix A substantively revise the eigenvalue/KL bound, replace argmax with max, and revise Gaussian normalization and the derived mean's sign. Main-text Theorem 1 and Definition 3 explicitly incorporate symmetry already assumed in v1's proof. Corrections remain inconsistent: v2's Corollary 1 gives a positive mean, whereas Equation 41 derives a negative mean.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the explicit claim about SAM's flatness advantage to IP alongside SWA and EMA. The central claims linking flatness to distributional robustness, reduced exposure bias, and quantization resilience remain, as does the claimed first systematic investigation.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 shifts emphasis toward 20-step benefits and attributes IP's weaknesses to undirected perturbations and suboptimal minima. New discussion identifies low-resolution evaluation as a limitation and suggests broader applications. Appendix B.3 interprets pEMA's FID improvements as insufficient for flatness or robustness; Remark 2 removes the claim that large parameter counts make bound terms negligible.

D1.justification: V2 documents pEMA's power-weighting and update equations and describes constructing adversarial inputs by maximizing diffusion loss. It expands the stated SWA scheduling information to FFHQ. These are limited technical additions; selected pEMA coefficients and detailed attack settings remain unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds references on post-hoc EMA, model compression, out-of-distribution generalization, and memorization. The related-work discussion replaces reinforcement-learning examples with compression connections and removes two reinforcement-learning references. The overall novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 revises portions of the motivation, background, results discussion, and related work; folds the former diffusion-model subsection into Section 2.2; and adds Discussion and Limitation, acknowledgments, and appendix subheadings. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains IP rows, while new Tables 5 and 7 and Figure 9 display added evidence. Existing figures are largely retained and repositioned. V1's appendix LSUN flatness Table 5 becomes v2's Table 6 with unchanged values; other layout changes mainly follow text reflow.

improvement.justification: Added IP/pEMA comparisons, fixed-seed 4-bit results, an adversarial test, and explicit low-resolution limitations make v2's evidence and scope more informative. Several mathematical corrections also help. The gain is limited by sparse specification of added experiments and incomplete propagation of theoretical corrections, particularly the conflicting Gaussian-mean signs in Corollary 1 and Equation 41.
